title: Dimensional Transformation & System Parameterisation
original:
Traditionally:

1. Input → 2. Output
or
1. Input → 2. Minor Edit → 3. Output

(ex. Direct system parameters manipulation (Co2, ppm) → Directly affected as output (Often as data visualisation))

What I propose (Especially for multi-user situations)

1. Input → 2. Input Dimensional Transformation → 3. System → 4. Output Dimensional Transformation → 5. Output

More precisely:

1. Input parameter adjustment interaction Input Modalities → 2. Input Dimensional Transformation (From UI Input parameters → System input parameters) → 3. Systematic Changes (System Input → System Output) → 4. Output Dimensional Transformation (System Output Parameters → User-facing Output parameters) → 5. Different A/V Output

For example:


1. Everyday Interface Input Modalities
1 → 2. Current parameters: Consumption, policy, traffic, real-world metrics
2. Input Dimensional Transformation (Real-world tangible action/data to system metrics)
2 → 3. Current parameters: Co2, PPM, (Ecological) System Input parameters 
3. Systematic Algorithm 
3 → 4. Current parameters: Temperature, Humidity, System Output parameters ‘Conseuqences’
4. Output Dimensional Transformation (System output to Real-world output/events)
4 → 5. Current parameters (Information): Wildfire/Natural Disaster, Lack of Water/Food Resources, etc.
5. Everyday Interface/Simulation/etc. Output 

1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5

Note: Dimensional Transformation is not 1:1 / 1:N / N:1 Relationship (i.e., not like single consumption/event directly transforming a single/multiple climate metric)

Rather, it’s a M:N Relationship → If there exist 7 input stations and 5 main climate metrics, for example, it’s a 7:5 relationship. Vice versa for the output dimensional transformation: Depicting a hyperobject can contaminate multiple outputs (코끼리와 장님).

This structure effectively captures the complexity and intertwining/relational structure of complex society/system/ecological system whilst well-managing/defining the algorithmic structure behind the scene.


WHY DIMENSIONAL TRANSFORMATION?

Direct configuration/parameterisation of the system, enabling suer to explicitly/directly control the system is not sexy at all --- Direct Manipulation, clear cause & effect가 되면 So What?
What is the value of interaction? More than just a simple interactive interface? Has clear limitations

Avoid direct manipulation. We need indeed DIMENSIONAL TRANSFORMATION btw interactions

차라리 Piano Interface 처럼 (피아노를 치는데 양쪽 스크린에서 시간이 조절된다?), 아니면 Toggler Interface/Toggler Interface + Voice INterface처럼 Multi-Modality Conducting? 한 Interactive Modality에서 다른 Systematic Parameter로 DIMENSIONAL TRANSFORMATION이 일어날때 진짜 재미가 느껴짐

Not obvious: Fun when the mental model is newly established. V-Effekt possible
Allows space for context to involve within the process of dimensional transformation

english:
Most interactive systems follow a familiar sequence: input, perhaps a small adjustment, then output. A participant changes a parameter such as carbon concentration, and a visualisation changes accordingly. I am interested in inserting transformations on both sides of the system: input, input dimensional transformation, system, output dimensional transformation, output.

A gesture first becomes a set of system parameters. The system processes them, and its consequences are translated again into something the audience encounters. In an ecological example, everyday actions concerning consumption, policy, or traffic could affect climate parameters; these could produce changes in temperature or humidity; those changes could then appear as altered resources, disasters, or everyday situations.

The mappings need not be one-to-one, one-to-many, or many-to-one. They can be many-to-many. Seven input stations might affect five climate variables, while a single systemic condition could manifest across many different outputs. Like the blind men encountering an elephant, each interface would disclose only part of something larger. This structure could articulate the entanglement of a social or ecological system while keeping its computational relationships explicitly defined.

Why introduce dimensional transformation? Direct parameter control can make cause and effect too obvious. Moving a slider and watching the corresponding graph change leaves me asking what the interaction contributes beyond access to a setting. A piano that changes time on surrounding screens, or a combination of switches and voice that conducts a system, asks participants to establish a different mental model.

This transformation is also where context can enter. Why a piano? Why a switch? Why a voice? Why should this particular bodily action produce that systemic change? A carefully chosen relationship can give the interaction an implicit conceptual layer. Its justification should become specific enough for someone to grasp and feel, rather than remain an explanation supplied afterwards.

This connects to the idea of the interface as an instrument. Instrumental input is translated into system input; the system produces consequences; those consequences are translated into an interface output. In a possible play garden, screaming, tapping, swiping, or other actions available to children could map into the nine planetary boundaries. The ecological model would then affect how the garden appears and behaves. Seven kinds of action might map into nine parameters, without each action belonging exclusively to one.

The structure resembles a simulation. Yet the question is not only whether the model reproduces a system. It is how the transformations around that model create an experience—and what kind of relationship they let us establish with it.
